chapters.title: Chapter 4: The Legal and Regulatory Framework

lessons.title: RERA in Plain English: What It Protects and What It Does Not

children.text: Before 2017, a homebuyer whose flat was three years late had two options: keep pleading with the builder, or spend a decade in consumer courts. RERA changed that. Today there is a regulator, a deadline and a legal right to interest or a refund. Yet in Noida and Mumbai, thousands of buyers hold RERA orders for refunds they have still not received. Both of these things are true at once. This lesson explains what RERA genuinely protects you from, and where its protection ends.

body.text: RERA gives buyers rights, disclosures and a regulator. It does not give guarantees: it cannot finish a stalled tower, find money a developer no longer has, or fix a title you never checked.

markDefs.definition: Under RERA, the developer or any person who builds or converts a building or land into apartments or plots for sale.
Under RERA, the buyer to whom a flat, plot or building has been allotted or sold by the promoter.
The state-level regulator set up under RERA to register projects and agents, hear complaints and pass orders.

children.text: RERA is the Real Estate (Regulation and Development) Act, 2016. It is a central law, but each state runs its own
, such as MahaRERA, UP RERA or K-RERA, and frames its own rules. Its core provisions came into force on 1 May 2017. The Act regulates the relationship between the
, and also requires real estate agents to register.

stats.label: States and UTs with a RERA authority
stats.context: As of September 2025; 29 had appellate tribunals

body.caption: RERA registration: who is in and who is out

cells: New project on land larger than 500 sq m
New project with more than 8 apartments, counting all phases
Project that was ongoing and had no completion certificate when RERA came into force
Plotted development meeting the size thresholds
Small project on 500 sq m or less with 8 apartments or fewer
No, unless the state lowers the threshold
Project that already had its completion certificate before RERA

Real estate agents selling registered projects

body.text: A developer cannot advertise, market, book or sell units in a project that must be registered but is not. Every advertisement must show the RERA registration number, and many states, including Maharashtra, also require a QR code linking to the project page. If a broker cannot show you a registration number, walk away.

body.caption: The main protections RERA gives buyers of registered projects

cells: Approvals, layout plans, land title details, completion date and the developer's past projects are uploaded to the RERA website
The developer must report construction progress and units sold every quarter
70% of buyer payments must go into a project account; withdrawals must be certified by an engineer, an architect and a chartered accountant
Flats must be sold on carpet area, not super built-up area
No more than 10% of the price can be taken before a registered agreement for sale
Sanctioned plans cannot be altered without the buyer's consent, and major changes need consent of two-thirds of allottees
If possession is late, withdraw with a full refund plus interest, or stay and receive interest for every month of delay
Structural defects and poor workmanship reported within 5 years of possession must be fixed free, within 30 days
Developers who break the rules can face penalties linked to the project's cost, and in some cases imprisonment

body.label: RERA's signature safeguard
body.value: 70% of buyer money kept in a separate project account
body.context: It exists because many developers once used advances from one project to buy land for the next, leaving earlier projects unfinished. Withdrawals must match the stage of construction and be certified by professionals.

children.text: Putting a Number on Delay Compensation

The interest rate for delays is set by each state's RERA rules, commonly linked to the SBI lending rate plus a margin. Buyers who stay in the project typically receive interest on the amount they have paid, for each month of delay. For illustration, assume a rate of 10% a year, calculated simply.

body.latex: \text{Delay Interest} = \text{Amount Paid} \times \text{Annual Interest Rate} \times \text{Years of Delay}
body.caption: A simplified version. Actual calculation depends on state rules, payment dates and the order passed.

children.text: Example: Nikhil has paid ₹60 lakh for a flat in Kharadi, Pune. Possession is 18 months late. At 10% a year, his delay interest is ₹60 lakh × 10% × 1.5 = ₹9 lakh.

body.title: Calculate delay interest
body.prompt: Shalini has paid ₹45 lakh for an under-construction flat in Gurugram. Possession is 2 years late, and the applicable interest rate is 10.5% a year, calculated simply. How much delay interest is she entitled to, in ₹ lakh? Round to two decimal places.
body.explanation: ₹45 lakh × 10.5% × 2 = ₹9.45 lakh. It is meaningful compensation, but it may not fully cover two years of rent plus EMIs, and it is only worth something if the developer actually pays.

children.text: Confirm the project and its promised completion date on the state RERA portal.
Send the developer a written notice, keeping copies of your agreement, payment receipts and correspondence.
Submit a complaint on the state RERA portal with the prescribed fee. Many buyers file without a lawyer.
The authority hears both sides and passes an order for refund, interest or possession. Claims for compensation go to the adjudicating officer.

markDefs.definition: An order issued when a developer does not pay a RERA award, allowing the amount to be recovered like land revenue arrears through the district administration, including by attaching the developer's property or bank accounts.

children.text: If the developer does not comply, the buyer seeks a
, which the district administration must execute.
Either side can appeal to the state's Real Estate Appellate Tribunal, generally within 60 days, and then to the High Court.

body.title: The common assumption vs the reality

columns.label: What buyers often assume
points: "RERA-registered means the project will be completed"
"A RERA refund order means I will get my money"

columns.label: The reality
points: Registration is not a guarantee; projects can still stall if the developer runs out of money
Orders must be enforced through district officials, and recovery can take years or fail
Developers disclose title documents; RERA does not certify that the title is clean
It mainly governs sales by promoters; a resale between individuals relies on your own due diligence
Completion dates can be extended, as authorities did for many projects during COVID-19

children.text: Enforcement is the biggest gap. RERA authorities can order a refund, but collecting it depends on revenue officials attaching and selling the developer's assets. When a developer enters insolvency proceedings, a moratorium usually halts recovery altogether, and buyers must instead file claims in the insolvency process.

body.caption: How two large RERA authorities have fared on recovery

cells: ₹1,505 crore through enforcement, plus ₹535 crore through settlements, for ₹2,040 crore of relief

body.title: MahaRERA: recovery ordered vs recovered (₹ crore, as reported)
What share got recovered?
body.prompt: MahaRERA reportedly recovered ₹268.87 crore against recovery orders of about ₹792 crore. What percentage of the ordered amount was recovered? Round to the nearest whole number.
body.explanation: ₹268.87 crore ÷ ₹792 crore = 0.339, or about 34%. Roughly two of every three rupees ordered had not reached buyers. Much of the stuck amount is linked to developers in insolvency, where recovery is legally paused.

body.text: The most valuable part of RERA is not the complaint process. It is the information available before you buy. A developer's past projects, delays, complaints against them, quarterly progress and approvals are all public on RERA portals. Preventing a bad purchase is far easier than recovering money after one.

events.title: RERA enacted by Parliament

body.title: Know your remedy
body.question: Imran's registered project in Thane is 20 months past the RERA completion date. He no longer wants the flat. What is he entitled to under RERA?
options: A refund of only the principal amount paid
A full refund of amounts paid, plus interest, along with any compensation the adjudicating officer awards
Automatic transfer of a different, completed flat
body.explanation: When a promoter fails to deliver on time, a buyer who withdraws is entitled to a refund with interest at the prescribed rate, and can seek compensation. The practical challenge is getting the developer to pay.

body.title: The ring-fence
body.textWithBlank: Under RERA, developers must deposit ___% of the money collected from buyers into a separate project bank account.
body.explanation: 70% must be kept in a separate account and used only for that project's land and construction costs, with withdrawals certified by an engineer, an architect and a chartered accountant.

body.title: The unpaid refund order
body.scenario: Rakesh booked a flat in Greater Noida West in 2018 and paid ₹52 lakh. The project stalled. In 2023, UP RERA ordered the developer to refund his money with interest. The developer did not pay. Rakesh obtained a recovery certificate, but in 2025 the developer was admitted into insolvency proceedings.
body.prompt: What does this mean for Rakesh, and what should he do now?
body.modelAnswer:
1. Recovery is paused: once insolvency proceedings begin, a moratorium generally stops recovery actions, including execution of his recovery certificate.
2. File a claim: Rakesh must file his claim, supported by his agreement, receipts and the RERA order, with the insolvency professional within the deadline announced.
3. Creditor status: homebuyers are treated as financial creditors in insolvency, voting as a class through an authorised representative on the resolution plan.
4. Likely outcomes: a resolution plan may complete the project and deliver flats, offer partial refunds, or in a worst case lead to liquidation. Timelines are often long.
5. Stay organised: he should join the homebuyers' group for the project, track the insolvency case and vote on the plan.
6. The lesson for other buyers: RERA orders are only as strong as the developer's finances. Checking the developer's track record, debt and complaint history on RERA portals before booking is the best protection.

body.title: Use RERA Before You Book, Not After
steps: Find the project on the state RERA portal using its registration number
Compare the RERA completion date with what the broker promised
Read the last few quarterly progress updates and check construction against them
Search for complaints and orders against the developer and its past projects
Download the approved plans and check carpet areas and amenities
Review land title and encumbrance disclosures, then have a lawyer verify them
Confirm the agent is registered with RERA
Pay no more than 10% before a registered agreement for sale

body.label: Unified National RERA Portal
body.description: Search RERA-registered projects across states from a single government portal, then check full details on the state RERA website.

cards.definition: The Real Estate (Regulation and Development) Act, 2016, enforced by state authorities from 1 May 2017.
The developer or person who builds or converts property into units for sale.
The buyer to whom a unit is allotted or sold by the promoter.
Projects on land over 500 sq m or with more than 8 apartments must register, unless a state sets lower limits.
70% of buyer money must be kept in a dedicated project account for land and construction costs.
An order allowing an unpaid RERA award to be recovered through the district administration.
The state body that hears appeals against RERA authority orders, with a further appeal to the High Court.

points: RERA is a central law enforced by state authorities, covering projects above 500 sq m or 8 apartments, and real estate agents.
Its protections include disclosure, quarterly updates, a 70% separate account, carpet area pricing, a 10% advance cap, delay interest or refunds, and 5-year defect liability.
Complaints can be filed online, with appeals to the Appellate Tribunal and then the High Court.
RERA does not guarantee completion or recovery: enforcement depends on district officials, and insolvency proceedings can freeze it.
Reported figures show MahaRERA recovering only about a third of the amounts it ordered.
Use RERA's public data before you book: developer track record, complaints, progress updates and approvals.

body.text: This lesson is for education only and is not legal or investment advice. RERA rules, interest rates, thresholds and procedures vary by state and change over time, and the case examples are illustrative. Consult a qualified property lawyer for any dispute, and a SEBI-registered investment adviser before making investment decisions.
